title: Protein structure generation via folding diffusion
layout_note: Top row: the diffusion chain as large open circles x_T -> ... -> x_t -> x_{t-1} -> ... -> x_0, the learned step p_xi(x_{t-1} | x_t) written above a solid arrow and the forward step q(x_t | x_{t-1}) under a dashed arrow curving back. Under the two ends of the chain, each state is shown twice: as an angle heatmap ('= x_T', 'x_0 =') and below it a rendered 'Corresponding structure' (a tangled green tube for x_T, a helical bundle for x_0). The bottom centre holds a ball-and-stick backbone schematic that defines the six angles.
grouping: No containers. Angle types are colour families in the schematic: dihedral torsions (phi, psi, omega) in orange with small dashed circular arrows around their bonds, bond angles (theta1-theta3) in dark green with dashed arcs. Atoms are white circles with letters, the carbonyl oxygen a blue circle, side chains R1/R2 grey rounded squares.
shapes_depth: Flat: open black-outlined circles for states, thin black arrows, a blue-green-yellow heatmap strip for each angle state, rendered green tube cartoons for structures. Math-italic labels; distributions written on the arrows.
proposed_highlight: No 'ours' block; what the method changes - the diffused variable is a set of backbone angles - is made the visual centre: the angle-definition schematic sits under the middle of the chain, and both chain ends show the angles as a heatmap with the structure they produce beneath.
lesson: When the generated variable is not coordinates, show each end of the chain twice - as the variable itself (a heatmap of angles per residue) and, below it, the 3-D structure it decodes to - and define the variable once in a small colour-coded chemical schematic between them.
notes: venue = arXiv: the PDF footer says 'Preprint. Under review.' (v2, 24 Nov 2022); no published venue was verified. year = arXiv preprint year (2209.15611). The heatmaps and structure renders are embedded images recorded by refs crop and left out of the palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: protein backbone generation via angle diffusion

core.what: The diffusion state is defined on a drawn protein backbone: a ball-and-stick chain at bottom centre with torsions phi/psi/omega (orange dashed circular arrows) and bond angles theta1-3 (green dashed arcs) marked where they act.

relations.form: a small backbone instance N - Ca - C - N - Ca with side groups R1/R2 and O, each of the six angles drawn at the bond or joint it measures
top row of large circles x_T -> ... -> x_t -> x_{t-1} -> ... -> x_0, with a solid learned reverse arrow p_xi and a dashed forward-noise arrow q bending back between x_t and x_{t-1}
under each end of the chain the same pair is drawn: an angle heatmap '= x_T' / 'x_0 =' and a rendered 'Corresponding structure' (tangle at left, helical bundle at right)

channels.colour: orange = torsion angles, dark green = bond angles; heatmaps use a viridis-like colormap for angle values; the green tube renders are a third green with no relation to the bond-angle green; light blue O and grey R are atom types
channels.shape: large open circle = diffusion state, small circle = atom, grey rounded square = side chain, heatmap = state as angle matrix, tube = 3-D structure
channels.line: solid arrow = learned reverse step, dashed curved arrow = forward noising; dashed arcs/circles = angles; thin black lines = bonds

quality.strengths: The representation (angles, not coordinates) is the visual centre and is drawn on the structure it parameterises; the two chain ends are shown as data in two forms (heatmap and rendered fold), making noise vs structure visible; forward vs reverse steps differ by line style.
quality.weaknesses: The backbone glyph sits between the two ends with no line tying it to x_t, so which state it describes is implicit; green is used for both bond angles and the protein renders; heatmap axes are unlabeled so the reader cannot tell rows are angles.

insights.structure: Top row is the diffusion chain x_T -> ... -> x_t -> x_{t-1} -> ... -> x_0 in large open circles; below each end sit an angle heatmap and a rendered structure, and the bottom centre holds a ball-and-stick backbone defining the six angles.
insights.data: States are shown three ways: as math circles, as angle heatmaps (noisy vs banded), and as green cartoon tubes (tangle vs helical bundle) labelled 'Corresponding structure'.
insights.emphasis: Torsions phi/psi/omega are orange with dashed circular arrows and bond angles theta1-3 dark green with dashed arcs, making the representation (angles, not coordinates) the visual centre.
insights.flow: Left-to-right along the chain with the learned reverse step p_xi as a solid arrow and the forward q as a dashed arrow curving back underneath; the lower content is read by column, not by arrows.
insights.avoid: The network that predicts the denoising step is never drawn, so the figure explains the representation but not the model.

arrangement.units: no frames; chain row on top, two state-illustration columns under its ends, angle-definition schematic in the bottom centre
arrangement.inputs_as: noise state x_T circle with its noisy heatmap and tangled structure below
